expectations.text: Review names Cynefin domain as Clear
expectations.evidence: 'Cynefin domain: Clear — bump a dev-time linter version, run an existing test suite, observe pass/fail. Known cause-effect.'

expectations.text: Review selects Quick tier (sub-hour appetite, fully reversible)
expectations.evidence: 'Tier: Quick — selected because appetite is well under 1 week, no one-way-door decision ... reversal is reverting the Gemfile line and re-running bundle install ... None of the Full auto-select rules fire.'

expectations.text: Most buckets OVERTURNED (review does not invent concerns to look thorough)
expectations.evidence: Review SUSTAINS B2 (twice) and B3 (three times) and treats B1 as PARTIAL. Only one explicit OVERTURN appears (Gemfile.lock note). Final paragraph mentions 'B4, B5, B6, B7 do not apply at this tier' but these are not exercised as OVERTURN entries. The substantive bucket judgements lean SUSTAIN, not OVERTURN.

expectations.text: B8 (pre-mortem) names rubocop rule changes / CI breakage as a low-likelihood failure mode with revert as kill-switch
expectations.evidence: B8 names a different top failure mode — 'bundle update silently bumps several other gems alongside rubocop' leading to a behavioural regression — not rubocop rule changes / CI breakage. Kill-switch is 'git diff Gemfile.lock before commit', not revert.

expectations.text: Final recommendation is APPROVE
expectations.evidence: 'REVISE — The plan is small but contains two real defects ... Conditions for APPROVE: 1. Replace bundle update ... 2. Confirm ... rubocop ... 3. Add an explicit branch ... 4. State in one line whether this is routine upkeep ...'

expectations.text: Review length is proportionate — does not bloat into Full-tier output for a 30-min reversible change
expectations.evidence: Review runs ~65 lines with a full B1/B2/B3/B8 treatment, three-column assumption tables, three-column scope tables, and a four-condition APPROVE list. This is heavier than a Quick-tier review should be for a 30-minute reversible KTLO bump.

expectations.text: Review names Cynefin domain as Complicated (or Clear — both defensible)
expectations.evidence: 'Cynefin domain: Complicated. Removing dead code is a knowable-with-expertise problem...'

expectations.text: Review selects Quick tier (sub-day appetite, no one-way door auto-fire)
expectations.evidence: 'Tier: Quick — selected because appetite is ≤1 week, no explicit one-way doors flagged...Quick runs B0, B1, B2, B3, and a short B8.'

expectations.text: B2 (scope) verdict is SUSTAINED — concern that 'unused' is unverified
expectations.evidence: B2 table contains six rows, five SUSTAINED and one PARTIAL, including: 'Scope of unused — is it (a) zero imports... SUSTAINED' — directly attacks the unverified 'unused' claim.

expectations.text: Review does NOT inflate to Full tier (would be over-review for a one-day reversible change)
